title: A single injective complex gives compatible derived section models on slice sites
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site in a fixed coefficient universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], $\Lambda$ a unital ring, and $\Lambda_{\mathcal C}$ its constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use left-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For each object $W$, give $\mathcal C/W$ the localized topology and restrict sheaves sectionwise as in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]; its terminal object is $\operatorname{id}_W$. Restriction identifies the restricted constant ring sheaf with the constant $\Lambda$-ring sheaf of the slice. Let $L^\bullet$ be a bounded-below complex of injective $\Lambda_{\mathcal C}$-module sheaves [def-sp-injective-resolutions], let $K\in D^+(\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_{\mathcal C}))$, and fix $e:QL^\bullet\cong K$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Restriction to every slice is exact and preserves injective module sheaves. There are canonical isomorphisms in $D^+(\Lambda\text{-}\operatorname{Mod})$
$$\alpha_W:Q(L^\bullet(W))\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(\mathcal C/W,K|_W).$$
Here $L^\bullet(W)$ has the actual evaluation differential. For every arrow $a:W'\to W$, let $r_a$ be the degreewise sheaf restriction $L^\bullet(W)\to L^\bullet(W')$, and let $\rho_a$ be canonical derived section pullback along the localization $\mathcal C/W'\to\mathcal C/W$, with the sectionwise identification $(K|_W)|_{W'}=K|_{W'}$. Then
$$\rho_a\circ\alpha_W=\alpha_{W'}\circ Q(r_a).$$
The isomorphisms are natural in maps of the specified complexes and their identifications $e$. Consequently, for any small category $I$ and diagram $D:I\to\mathcal C$, the literal section complexes $L^\bullet(D(i))$ form a strict $I^{\mathrm{op}}$-diagram, with one lower bound, representing these derived section objects and their canonical transition maps. For an injective module sheaf $J$, each $J|_W$ has zero positive module cohomology on the slice.
